title: What 6 months of using AI to make a game looks like for me
author: VelocityVendettaGame
selftext:
Hi everyone. I am the developer of Velocity Vendetta, a commercial game currently being developed in Unreal Engine 5. The attached seven-minute video shows gameplay from its two modes: Velocity League, which focuses on car soccer, and Vendetta Arena, which focuses on vehicle combat. I was very nostalgic and miss those games like twisted metal and vigilante 8 so i created it myself along with car soccer because i thought why not, i have the cars and some mechanics.

  
I started with claude code 0 experience and had bought a vehicle arcade system to get the hang of unreal and driving etc and then i tried to do blueprints with AI and took like 3-4 days to get what i wanted and with vfx to prove a concept. After, i tried to compare to working with C++ and claude code and was so much faster and recreated what i did in C++ in about half a day. I then put together all the info regarding my game into notion to gather my thoughts and be able to give AI the full scope of what i plan to build because all of you know, if you don't plan ahead for it. it's hard to rework which i learned the hardway when i transitioned from chaos physiscs to jolt physics engine in unreal 5 for reliable networking. So to build my plan, i had used gemini, gpt and claude to recommend and argue with each other on best plan and i did this at each major phase like determinism and networking (car soccer fully working) and when they decided on best planned structure i implemented with claude code then i was working 4 hours doing 1-2 weapons daily and i would use the plan that i had to have gpt prompt claude code for me for the best prompt engineering. Each weapon has 4 combos so that's why it took a while but i did get faster from 1 weapon half a day as i got comfortable with the system. I did this too when i went to implement sound and only implemented my engine sound which i then decided i am going to hire a sound engineer to do the rest as it's an art for sure and for my VFX.  

Meanwhile all this, i had used gpt and gemini to create concepts of the cars i wanted for my game and hired a 3d artist to make my cars which you can see on my website the other cars (5 or 6? of them so far)

I then realized for networking i needed better physics engine for the level i want my game to be so i migrated it all to jolt and that was a month of learning curve and eventually a month later i had a working networking game for my velocity league (soccer). I switched from claude code to chat gpt as my main source and used claude code to review and audit and for second opinions but that was because with chatgpt sol 5.6 fixed in 2 prompts what fable 5 couldn't in 4 days of work. I tested it with friends and to audit both our files, it would auto create files for me to give to chatgpt to audit and make the small fine retouches and refinements and works good now. Now i am just refining all my game mechanics for velocity league which i learned auto creating files for review was a good way for small touches of refinement and vendetta arena my combat i will finish my vfx as i had put that on hold because iwanted to see if i could get my networking to work with car soccer as that would prove my car combat would work just fine too and so now i am focusing on it to finish vfx and going through my 40 different combos and adding my ultimates as well per car.

[velocityvendetta.com](http://velocityvendetta.com)

comments.author: Fusionism
comments.body:
It looks nice but why did you make an exact clone of rocket league? Why would you do this? At the very least if you're using AI, come up with your own original idea, you could have made anything, but you just made a copy of an already widely popular game, if it was just to learn that's fine, but if you plan on marketing and selling this,  which is seems like you do you're absolutely cooked.

Let's assume just for fun Psyonix lawyers don't take you down instantly and with overwhelming force (And they will, and they will easily win), no one will play this because Rocket League is simply better and more popular, by orders of magnitude.

replies.author: VelocityVendettaGame
replies.body: It's somewhat different. Not the same, there are a few things different and the way I am building trading too so that if you play either game mode of car combat or car soccer. That's like saying battle royals or all extraction shooters or like Nintendo who lost to pal world are the same. They don't own the rights to car soccer. Competition is healthy

replies.author: Fusionism
replies.body:
I agree that they don't own the rights to car soccer, and concepts like that should not be copyrightable. But I'd implore you to do some research on this famous legal case: **Tetris Holding v. Xio Interactive** 

Your recreation here is completely the same, you neglected to make anything new other than claiming to slap on "car combat" mechanics which was not visible in video, and trading which was already in Rocket League. You didn't try to distinguish it at all, you're even using the same orange vs blue colors that Rocket League uses for the opposing teams. Same 5 minute score board, same transparent netted arena walls with a ceiling, same boost placement.

It's an affront to creativity. You didn't make any other expressive choices in the design, you simply did what Rocket League did.

I really hope you read about the case above I mentioned. And if you still want to continue I think you really should go ahead with it, because you'll learn a lot honestly, and at best you'll have to redesign your entire project from the ground up.

replies.author: VelocityVendettaGame

But yeah I'll look into it thanks!
